bookreview.text: In books_info, "description", "categories" and "features" look like lists or dictionaries but are stored as strings.
"book_id" in books_info and "purchase_id" in review refer to the same books, although the field names differ.
Joining books_info.book_id to review.purchase_id needs a fuzzy join: the values do not match exactly.
Some queries need information from the "categories" or "details" columns of books_info.

crmarenapro.text: About 25% of ID-like fields include a leading # (e.g. #001Wt00000PFj4zIAD).
About 20% of text fields contain trailing whitespace (e.g. "Company Name ").
The corruption appears in the fields Id, AccountId, ContactId, Name, FirstName, LastName, Email, Subject and Status.
Handling the corruption is needed for reliable joins.

DEPS_DEV_V1.text: Package records in packageinfo (package_database) match records in project_packageversion (project_database) on System, Name and Version.
ProjectName in project_packageversion finds the corresponding record in project_info.
The Project_Information field of project_info holds the project name and repository metrics such as GitHub stars and fork counts, with other descriptive details.

GITHUB_REPOS.text: Tables are joined on identifiers such as "id" or "repo_name".
The languages table's language_description field may list several programming languages for one repository.
A repository's primary language is the one with the most bytes.
The contents table's repo_data_description field is natural-language metadata derived from file attributes (size, binary, copies, mode).
Some queries rely on the attributes in repo_data_description for filtering or interpretation.

PANCANCER_ATLAS.text: The average log10-transformed expression value is the mean of log10(normalized_count + 1) across samples.
Molecular data match clinical_info by its "Patient_description" and the molecular data's "ParticipantBarcode".
clinical_info's "Patient_description" holds more about each patient, such as uuid, barcode, gender and vital status.
The chi-square statistic is the sum over cells of (O - E)^2 / E, with E = row total * column total / grand total.
LGG means brain lower grade glioma; BRCA means breast invasive carcinoma.

googlelocal.text: The two databases join on the gmap_id field, combining reviews with business metadata.
Needed information can be in the "description" column of business_database.

music_brainz_20k.text: The tracks table has duplicates: different track_ids can be the same real-world track.
Duplicate tracks need not match exactly (e.g. different year formats or small attribute differences), so they are resolved by comparing title, artist, album, year and so on.
The sales table records sales in five countries: USA, UK, Canada, Germany and France.
Sales occur on five platforms or stores: iTunes, Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music and Google Play.

stockindex.text: The Exchange field in indexinfo_database holds full exchange names (e.g. "Tokyo Stock Exchange"), while the Index field in indextrade_database holds index symbols (e.g. "N225", "HSI", "000001.SS").
Joining the two needs each exchange matched to its major index symbol (e.g. Tokyo Stock Exchange to N225, Hong Kong Stock Exchange to HSI).
An exchange's region (Asia, Europe, North America) is not stored and must be inferred from geography (e.g. N225 is in Asia).
An up day is a trading day whose close is above its open; a down day one whose close is below its open.
Average intraday volatility is (High - Low) / Open per day, averaged over the period.

stockmarket.text: Listing exchange codes: A = NYSE MKT, N = NYSE, P = NYSE ARCA, Z = BATS, V = IEXG, Q = NASDAQ Global Select Market.

Financial status codes: D = deficient, E = delinquent, Q = bankrupt, N = normal, G = deficient and bankrupt, H = deficient and delinquent, J = delinquent and bankrupt, K = deficient, delinquent and bankrupt.
A company is financially troubled if it is deficient, delinquent, or both.
Market category codes: Q = NASDAQ Global Select Market, G = NASDAQ Global Market, S = NASDAQ Capital Market.
